newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stock trading limits to be reviewed Friday.
newsitem.headline: Thai stock trading limits to be reviewed Friday.

text.p: Stock Exchange of Thailand (SET) officials will meet brokers on Friday to discuss relaxing daily trading limits on stocks, exchange officials said on Thursday.
Stocks are currently allowed to trade within a 10 percent ceiling or floor based on the previous day's closing price.

"The Association of Securities Companies will meet with the SET president at noon on Friday to decide whether to implement this measure," head of the exchange's examinations department Sopawadee Lertmanachai said on Thursday.
"If our members are ready to do this it could happen next week," she said.

Many Thai stocks, which have soared over the last two days following a flotation and de facto devaluation of the currency on Wednesday, were stuck on their 10 percent daily ceilings and orders could not be completed, brokers said.
A change is unlikely to see stocks allowed to trade freely but may see the daily limits widened, brokers said.
Large local brokers generally favour relaxed trading limits although smaller firms have reservations about the increased risks it may pose to small investors, Sopawadee said.
